title: Pooled Remittances, Returns and Refunds on Payoff Cases
content:
Payoff funds on a Payoff and Loan Satisfaction case are pooled, whoever sends them.

**Pooling.** Funds from several remitters on one case, such as several heirs, a title company or a new lender, are pooled. The net amount remitted on a case is every payoff funds receipt on the case less every returned receipt on the case, over the life of the case up to and including the handling date. The case is funded when that net amount reaches the required payoff amount.

**Accepted methods.** Funds are accepted only by a method the plan lists among its accepted remittance methods. A personal check is never accepted, as the plan's personal-check setting provides, and is sent back without being recorded as a receipt.

**Recording each remittance.** **No longer in force.** The clause under which each remittance is recorded once, identified by its remittance reference, is no longer in force as worded here; it has been superseded by the current basis for recording remittances.

**Recalled and dishonored funds.** A recalled wire or dishonored check is returned against its receipt on the day Cedarline learns of it, as the plan's dishonored-funds handling provides, and the shortfall reopens.

**Short funds.** Funds that still fall short of the required amount the plan's short-funds holding period of calendar days after the first receipt are returned receipt by receipt to each original remitter.

**Application and refund on satisfaction.** **No longer in force.** The clause under which exactly the required payoff amount is applied on satisfaction and any held excess is refunded within the plan's refund period, first to the remitter of the receipt that took the pooled total over the required amount, up to that receipt's amount, and then to earlier remitters in reverse order of receipt, is no longer in force as worded here; it has been superseded by the current basis for applying and refunding funds.

**Held excess.** The excess held on a case is the net amount remitted less the required payoff amount, and never less than zero.

### Hypothetical pooling illustration

| Hypothetical entry | Amount |
|---|---|
| Wire from a first heir | USD 40000.00 |
| Cashier's check from a second heir | USD 25000.00 |
| Return of the cashier's check after it was dishonored | USD 25000.00 |
| Net amount remitted | USD 40000.00 |

Against a hypothetical required payoff amount of USD 60000.00 this case is not funded; the shortfall of USD 20000.00 is open again. Against a hypothetical required amount of USD 38000.00 it is funded and the held excess is USD 2000.00. All amounts are invented for the illustration.

superseded_clauses: Each remittance is recorded once, identified by its remittance_reference.

On satisfaction exactly the required payoff amount is applied to the loan, per funds_application_timing; any held excess is refunded within overpayment_refund_business_days business days to the remitter of the receipt that took the pooled total over the required amount, up to that receipt's amount, and then to earlier remitters in reverse order of receipt, per remitter_refund_target.
